key_insight: Strain gradients can break crystal symmetry and activate otherwise forbidden nonlinear optical responses in centrosymmetric materials.
engineering_relevance: Strain-gradient engineering could enable light conversion and photovoltaic responses in silicon and other centrosymmetric materials for nanoscale optoelectronics.
method: Develop a first-principles framework for flexo-photoresponses.
Map strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons using electron–phonon coupling theory.
Capture nonlocal quantum-mechanical effects on nonlinear optical responses.
evidence_signal: Calculations for silicon, cubic SrTiO3, and monolayer black phosphorus show that strain gradients of 10^5–10^6 m⁻¹ can induce second-harmonic generation and bulk photovoltaic responses comparable to intrinsic responses in non-centrosymmetric crystals.
watch_item: The abstract reports theoretical results, not experimental validation or solar-cell efficiency gains; generating and controlling the required strain gradients remains an implementation concern.
